head.title: Cache meter for Claude Code
head.subtitle: A Claude Code status line with the omp cache meter's countdown, cost and /compact advice, reusing its meter code.
head.tldr: Ship `claude-cache-meter`, an npm CLI that Claude Code runs as its status line. It shows variant D (the one-line meter), the expiry countdown, the /compact advice and the Tern pane state, all from the existing `meter.ts` and `view.ts`. 7 steps. 7 questions need a pick. The /compact advice ships only once step 2 has measured what Claude Code's compaction costs.

sections.title: Context
sections.lead: The meter only runs inside omp. Claude Code can't load extensions, but every time it updates its status line it gives that command enough data to draw the meter.

sections.title: Approach
sections.lead: One bundled Node script parses the stdin JSON plus any new transcript lines, updates the shared `Tracker` and prints the meter as ANSI lines.

sections.lead: 7 steps. The shared meter changes first (wording, host profile), so omp is proven unchanged before any Claude Code code depends on it.

249d22f605530909.md:
The omp extension rebuilds a `Tracker` from omp's session branch (`omp-extension/index.ts:59`). `snapshot()` turns it into what the meter shows (`omp-extension/meter.ts:176`), and `toAnsi()` draws it (`omp-extension/view.ts:166`). For Tern, `publish()` writes `panes/<TERN_PANE>.json` (`omp-extension/index.ts:74`).

Some parts assume omp:
- **Cache warmer:** the `Env.warmingMode` field (`meter.ts:111`).
- **Compaction cost model:** omp's own model (`SUMMARY_TOKENS`, `LONG_WRITE_FACTOR`, `keepRecentTokens`, `meter.ts:33-35`).
- **Prices:** taken from `model.cost` (`meter.ts:104`).
- **Settings file:** fixed at `~/.omp/agent/cache-meter.json` (`settings.ts:5`).

Claude Code has no extension API, and plugins can't set the main status line (only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine`). What Claude Code does have is a `statusLine` command, which gets this JSON on stdin each time it runs (docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline). Claude Code 2.1.302 is installed here, and `~/.claude/settings.json` has no `statusLine` yet.

| The meter needs | Claude Code provides |
|---|---|
| Warm or cold, expiry, TTL | `prompt_cache.warm`, `expires_at`, `ttl` (since v2.1.251) |
| Last request's read / write / uncached split | `context_window.current_usage` |
| Size of the next rebuild | `prompt_cache.recache_tokens_if_cold` |
| Misses and their cause | `prompt_cache.misses`, `last_miss_cause` |
| Request history and compactions | Transcript JSONL at `transcript_path`: each assistant message carries `message.usage`, split into `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h/5m`; each compaction leaves a `system/compact_boundary` entry with `compactMetadata.preTokens/postTokens` (seen in a real transcript here) |
| Per-token prices | None. `cost.total_cost_usd` is only the session total at list price; the `modelPricing` setting overrides it |
| Terminal width | `COLUMNS` environment variable |

How Claude Code compacts differs from omp (docs: prompt-caching, section "Compacting the conversation"):
- The summary request repeats the system prompt, the tools and the history.
- On a cold cache it sends that history as **uncached input**; omp writes it to the cache instead.
- The summary request uses the 5-minute TTL.
- On a 1-hour TTL, Claude Code may also compact an idle conversation on its own (`idleCompaction`).
- **No cache warmer:** none is documented, so I assume Claude Code has none (unverified).

items.md: The `statusLine.command` in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code runs it with the session JSON on stdin and shows what it prints, re-running it on new messages, after `/compact`, at cache expiry and every `refreshInterval` seconds.
The part of `Env` that differs per host: whether a cache warmer exists, how a cold compaction's summary request is billed, and how much recent conversation a compaction keeps.
Anthropic's API price per token. On a Claude subscription, usage within the plan is not billed per token, so dollars at list price are a comparison, not a bill.

14dff9a5a4be2534.md: The badge becomes coloured text. Colours are the terminal's 16 named ANSI colours, so they follow its theme: green for warm, yellow for expiring, red for cold, cyan for compacted, dim for secondary text. Bars use `━`. The second line, about the compaction, uses the reworded text from step 1.

items.title: Reword the compaction result in the shared meter
items.md:
Today `saved 455.7k tokens (~$0.74 net)` reads as if 455.7k tokens bought only $0.74.
- **Meter line:** `~$X cheaper per turn` (removed tokens × cache-read price), then `paid for itself (~$0.74)` or `cost ~$0.11 more`. The size stays only as `518.2k → 62.5k`.
- **`/cache` panel:** gets the breakdown as rows: rebuild avoided, summary request, first write after it, net.
- **Reach:** both hosts get this, through `compactAdvice()` and `renderMeter()`.

items.title: Measure what Claude Code's compaction costs on a cold cache
items.md:
I haven't found how the summary request's usage is recorded: the `compact_boundary` entry carries `preTokens`, `postTokens` and `durationMs`, but no usage (seen in one transcript).

**Method:**
1. Compact a throwaway session after its cache has expired.
2. Read `cost.total_cost_usd` before and after.
3. Compare that with `preTokens` × input price + output.

The results go into the Claude Code host profile: how the summary request is billed (uncached input, per the docs) and how many tokens survive (`postTokens`).

items.title: Make `meter.ts` host-neutral with a host profile
items.md:
- **`Env`:** gains `host: { warmer: boolean; summaryBilledAs: "write" | "input"; keepRecentTokens: number }`. omp passes today's values, so its output doesn't change.
- **`snapshot()` and `renderMeter()`:** skip the warming text when `warmer` is false.
- **Settings:** `loadSettings`/`saveSettings` take the file path; Claude Code uses `~/.claude/cache-meter.json`.
- **Tern state:** `publish()`'s body moves to `omp-extension/tern.ts`, so both hosts write the same v1 file with a new `host` field.

items.title: Add the `claude-code/` package: stdin adapter, transcript tail, prices
items.md:
- **`session.ts`:**
  - Reads the stdin JSON and catches up on the transcript from the stored offset. Only main-conversation assistant messages count; sidechains are skipped.
  - Records each one with `Tracker.record()`, and marks `compact_boundary` entries as compactions.
  - Saves the state atomically (tmp file + rename).
  - Live fields win over replayed ones: `prompt_cache.expires_at`, `ttl`, `warm` and `recache_tokens_if_cold`.
- **`prices.ts`:** Claude list prices per model, plus the 1-hour write multiplier. The user's `modelPricing` takes precedence. For an unknown model the meter shows tokens and no dollars.
- **`cli.ts`:** with stdin piped, prints `toAnsi(renderMeter(…), ansiTheme, COLUMNS)`.
- **Build:** `bun build --target node` produces `dist/claude-cache-meter.js`, the package's `bin`.
- **Typecheck:** the root `check` also covers `claude-code/src`.

items.title: Add `install`, `uninstall` and `panel` subcommands
items.md:
- **`install`:** writes `statusLine` (`command`, `refreshInterval` from question 3) into `~/.claude/settings.json`, keeping a `.bak` copy. If a `statusLine` already exists, it stops and prints both commands.
- **`uninstall`:** removes only a `statusLine` that it wrote itself.
- **`panel`:** prints `renderPanel()` for the newest session in the current directory. Claude Code has no command that shows output without spending a turn, so the panel lives in the CLI and in Tern's canvas.

items.title: Show Claude Code agents in the Tern plugin
items.md:
- **Wording:** "omp agent" becomes "agent", and the canvas shows the host next to the model.
- **Warming:** the warming column and `skipWarmed` ignore agents whose host has no warmer.
- **Compact button:** `cx.agents:ask(pane, "/compact")` must reach a Claude Code pane. That is unverified; if it doesn't work, the button is hidden for those agents.
- **`TERN_PANE`:** the status line command should inherit it from the pane (unverified).

items.title: Document and publish `claude-cache-meter` 0.1.0
items.md:
- **Docs:** a README for the package, and a Claude Code section in the root README with a screenshot.
- **Release:** `npm publish --access public` from `claude-code/`. Both `claude-cache-meter` and `cc-cache-meter` are free on npm (404 on `npm view` today). Publishing needs your npm login.

items.text: What does a Claude subscription user see instead of billed dollars?
items.sub: Recommend list-price dollars, labelled: they still rank continue vs /compact.

choices.label: Dollars, marked list price
choices.md: A subscription is detected when `rate_limits` is present; the dollars then read `≈$0.21 list`. Advice works the same; the label says it isn't a bill.

choices.label: Tokens only
choices.md: No dollars on a subscription; rebuilds show as `518k to re-cache`. The /compact advice then compares tokens, which ignores that writes cost more than reads.

choices.label: A setting, default dollars
choices.md: Same as list-price dollars, plus a `currency: tokens` switch in `cache-meter.json`. One more setting to document.

items.text: At what interval should the countdown redraw?
items.sub: Recommend every second, if a run measures under 60 ms.

choices.label: Every second
choices.md: `refreshInterval: 1`: the clock ticks like omp's. Each idle session starts Node once a second (about 40 ms of CPU, unmeasured).

choices.label: Every 10 seconds
choices.md: A tenth of the CPU; the clock jumps in 10-second steps, which is coarse in the last minute.

choices.label: Only on Claude Code events
choices.md: No timer: redraws on messages, `/compact` and at expiry. Between them the countdown is frozen, so it reads as remaining time at the last update.

items.text: How does the status line get configured?
items.sub: Recommend an `install` command that never overwrites an existing status line.

choices.label: install command
choices.md: `claude-cache-meter install` edits `~/.claude/settings.json` with a backup and stops when a `statusLine` exists. One command, but the tool edits your settings file.

choices.label: README snippet only
choices.md: You paste the JSON yourself. Nothing touches your settings, and there's one manual step with room for typos.

choices.label: install that wraps
choices.md: An existing status line is kept and printed above the meter (`--then "<old command>"`). Keeps your current line, but adds its runtime to every refresh.

choices.md: `npx claude-cache-meter install` installs the package globally and writes `statusLine` with a `.bak` backup. If a status line already exists, it stops instead of overwriting. Updates come from `npm update -g`, and the command path stays the same.

choices.label: Both
choices.md: The npm package as above, plus a plugin whose setup skill runs `npx claude-cache-meter install`. Two things to publish and keep in step, for the convenience of `claude plugin install`.

replies.md: There's no `claude install <package>`: `claude install` only installs Claude Code itself. Its installer is `claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace>`, after `claude plugin marketplace add <repo>`. But a plugin can't set the main status line (only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine`), so some step still has to edit settings.json. I've rewritten the options below to say exactly what each one does.

items.text: What does the meter advise on a cold Claude Code cache?
items.sub: Your call: always /compact. Claude Code bills the cold summary as plain input, so it wins.

choices.label: Always /compact when cold
choices.md: No payback calculation for Claude Code. The dollar figures stay as information, and `advice.paybackTurns` applies to omp only. Step 2's measurement only sharpens the `paid for itself` amount.

choices.label: Sizes, no advice
choices.md: The meter shows `518.2k → 62.5k` and the rebuild cost, and recommends nothing until it has a measurement.

replies.md: Agreed, for Claude Code. On a cold cache, Claude Code sends the history to the summary request as uncached input (1× the input price). Continuing instead rewrites the whole prefix at 1.25× (5-minute TTL) or 2× (1-hour TTL). At 518k tokens, compacting costs about 518k input + ~3k output + 62k written, against 518k written at 1.25× or 2×: cheaper right away, before counting the cheaper turns after it. omp is different: its summary request writes the history to the cache, so omp keeps its payback rule.

items.title: Measure what Claude Code's compaction costs on a cold cache
items.md:
How the summary request's usage gets recorded is still unknown: the `compact_boundary` entry carries `preTokens`, `postTokens` and `durationMs`, but no usage (seen in one transcript). The /compact advice no longer depends on this step; on a cold cache it is always /compact. This step only sharpens the `paid for itself` amount.

**Method:**
1. Compact a throwaway session after its cache has expired.
2. Read `cost.total_cost_usd` before and after.
3. Compare that with `preTokens` × input price + output.

The results go into the Claude Code host profile.

items.title: Make `meter.ts` host-neutral with a host profile
items.md:
- **`Env`:** gains `host: { warmer: boolean; summaryBilledAs: "write" | "input"; coldAdvice: "payback" | "always"; keepRecentTokens: number }`. omp passes today's values, so its output doesn't change. Claude Code passes `coldAdvice: "always"`.
- **`snapshot()` and `renderMeter()`:** skip the warming text when `warmer` is false.
- **Settings:** `loadSettings`/`saveSettings` take the file path; Claude Code uses `~/.claude/cache-meter.json`.
- **Tern state:** `publish()`'s body moves to `omp-extension/tern.ts`, so both hosts write the same v1 file with a new `host` field.

items.title: Add the `claude-code/` package: stdin adapter, transcript tail, prices
items.md:
- **`session.ts`:**
  - Reads the stdin JSON and catches up on the transcript from the stored offset. Only main-conversation assistant messages count; sidechains are skipped.
  - Records each one with `Tracker.record()`, and marks `compact_boundary` entries as compactions.
  - Saves the state atomically (tmp file + rename).
  - Live fields win over replayed ones: `prompt_cache.expires_at`, `ttl`, `warm` and `recache_tokens_if_cold`.
- **`prices.ts`:** Claude list prices per model, plus the 1-hour write multiplier. The user's `modelPricing` takes precedence. For an unknown model the meter shows tokens and no dollars.
- **`cli.ts`:** with stdin piped, prints `toAnsi(renderMeter(…), ansiTheme, COLUMNS)`.
- **Build:** `bun build --target node` produces `dist/claude-cache-meter.js`, the package's `bin`.
- **Typecheck:** the root `check` also covers `claude-code/src`.

items.title: Add `install`, `uninstall` and `panel` subcommands
items.md:
- **`install`:** writes `statusLine` (`command`, `refreshInterval` from question 3) into `~/.claude/settings.json`, keeping a `.bak` copy. If a `statusLine` already exists, it stops and prints both commands.
- **`uninstall`:** removes only a `statusLine` that it wrote itself.
- **`panel`:** prints `renderPanel()` for the newest session in the current directory. Claude Code has no command that shows output without spending a turn, so the panel lives in the CLI and in Tern's canvas.

items.title: Show Claude Code agents in the Tern plugin
items.md:
- **Wording:** "omp agent" becomes "agent", and the canvas shows the host next to the model.
- **Warming:** the warming column and `skipWarmed` ignore agents whose host has no warmer.
- **Compact button:** `cx.agents:ask(pane, "/compact")` must reach a Claude Code pane. That is unverified; if it doesn't work, the button is hidden for those agents.
- **`TERN_PANE`:** the status line command should inherit it from the pane (unverified).

items.title: Document and publish `claude-cache-meter` 0.1.0
items.md:
- **Docs:** a README for the package, and a Claude Code section in the root README with a screenshot.

items.text: Where does the Claude Code version live?
items.sub: Recommend this repo, own package: one copy of meter.ts, two installs.

choices.label: claude-code/ in this repo
choices.md: A second npm package that bundles `meter.ts` and `view.ts` at build time. A fix to the meter reaches both hosts in one commit; the omp package's contents don't change.

choices.label: Separate repo
choices.md: Its own issues and stars, but `meter.ts` and `view.ts` are copied, and every fix has to be made twice.

choices.label: One npm package for both
choices.md: One name to install, but omp users download the Claude Code bundle and the other way round, and the package's root layout has to satisfy both hosts.

items.text: What does a Claude subscription user see instead of billed dollars?
items.sub: Recommend list-price dollars, labelled: they still rank continue vs /compact.

choices.label: Dollars, marked list price
choices.md: A subscription is detected when `rate_limits` is present; the dollars then read `≈$0.21 list`. Advice works the same; the label says it isn't a bill.

choices.label: Tokens only
choices.md: No dollars on a subscription; rebuilds show as `518k to re-cache`. The /compact advice then compares tokens, which ignores that writes cost more than reads.

choices.label: A setting, default dollars
choices.md: Same as list-price dollars, plus a `currency: tokens` switch in `cache-meter.json`. One more setting to document.

items.text: At what interval should the countdown redraw?
items.sub: Recommend every second, if a run measures under 60 ms.

choices.label: Every second
choices.md: `refreshInterval: 1`: the clock ticks like omp's. Each idle session starts Node once a second (about 40 ms of CPU, unmeasured).

choices.label: Every 10 seconds
choices.md: A tenth of the CPU; the clock jumps in 10-second steps, which is coarse in the last minute.

choices.label: Only on Claude Code events
choices.md: No timer: redraws on messages, `/compact` and at expiry. Between them the countdown is frozen, so it reads as remaining time at the last update.

items.text: How does the status line get installed?
items.sub: Recommend `npx claude-cache-meter install`: one command, and updates don't break the path.

choices.label: npx … install
choices.md: `npx claude-cache-meter install` installs the package globally and writes `statusLine` with a `.bak` backup. If a status line already exists, it stops instead of overwriting. Updates come from `npm update -g`, and the command path stays the same.

choices.label: Claude Code plugin
choices.md: Two commands: `claude plugin marketplace add andreiverdes/omp-cache-meter`, then `claude plugin install cache-meter@omp-cache-meter`, plus a `/cache-meter:setup` skill. Claude then edits `settings.json` for you, which costs one turn. The script runs from the plugin cache, whose path may contain the version (unverified), so an update could leave `statusLine` pointing at a deleted folder.

choices.label: Both
choices.md: The npm package as above, plus a plugin whose setup skill runs `npx claude-cache-meter install`. Two things to publish and keep in step, for the convenience of `claude plugin install`.

replies.md: There's no `claude install <package>`: `claude install` only installs Claude Code itself. Its installer is `claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace>`, after `claude plugin marketplace add <repo>`. But a plugin can't set the main status line (only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine`), so some step still has to edit settings.json. I've rewritten the options below to say exactly what each one does.

items.text: Reword the compaction result for both hosts (step 1)?
items.sub: Recommend yes: the current line reads as if 455.7k tokens bought only $0.74.

choices.label: Yes, as in the compare
choices.md: `~$0.09 cheaper per turn · paid for itself (~$0.74)` on the meter line, plus the breakdown in the panel. Changes omp screenshots in the README.

choices.label: Keep the current text
choices.md: No change to omp. Claude Code inherits the same confusing line.

items.text: When does omp-cache-meter 0.1.0 go to npm?
items.sub: Recommend after step 1, so the first npm release has the clearer wording.

choices.label: Now, as committed
choices.md: Publish `a73e1ea` once you're logged in to npm; the wording fix becomes 0.1.1.

choices.label: After step 1
choices.md: The amended initial commit and tag `v0.1.0` gain the wording fix, then publish. A day's delay at most.

choices.label: With the Claude Code release
choices.md: Both packages ship on the same day with the shared refactor. omp users wait for the whole plan.

items.text: What does the meter advise on a cold Claude Code cache?
items.sub: Your call: always /compact. Claude Code bills the cold summary as plain input, so it wins.

choices.label: Always /compact when cold
choices.md: No payback calculation for Claude Code. The dollar figures stay as information, and `advice.paybackTurns` applies to omp only. Step 2's measurement only sharpens the `paid for itself` amount.

choices.label: Sizes, no advice
choices.md: The meter shows `518.2k → 62.5k` and the rebuild cost, and recommends nothing until it has a measurement.

replies.md: Agreed, for Claude Code. On a cold cache, Claude Code sends the history to the summary request as uncached input (1× the input price). Continuing instead rewrites the whole prefix at 1.25× (5-minute TTL) or 2× (1-hour TTL). At 518k tokens, compacting costs about 518k input + ~3k output + 62k written, against 518k written at 1.25× or 2×: cheaper right away, before counting the cheaper turns after it. omp is different: its summary request writes the history to the cache, so omp keeps its payback rule.
